title: OpenPartsCore material attributes (schema v0)
description: What `attributes` holds for an entry in the `material` namespace (ADR-0007). One layout: `identity` (what the product is), `spool_rfid` (what the printer read off the spool tag), `tds` (the vendor's technical data sheet, every table row verbatim with its page), `normalised` (typed values transcribed from `tds` or from `spool_rfid`, each naming its page or its basis), `marketing_claims` (store-page text kept only so a claim can be traced) and `review` (status and the flags a reviewer must read). Numbers are transcribed, never converted: a key's unit is in its name. Absent means unknown, never zero. Citation strings are checked by scripts/validate.py, not here.

polymer.description: Base polymer as the vendor names it: PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, TPU, PA, PC ...

item_numbers.description: Vendor item number per colour or variant, as printed on the cited page.

spool_rfid.description: Fields as the printer reported them from the spool's RFID tag. Field names are the tag's own (minTemp, maxTemp, pressure), preserved verbatim and not interpreted.

note.description: Which printer, which slot, which day, and what is not interpreted.

tds.description: The vendor TDS as printed. Fixed keys are the document's identity, its Items tables and its storage text; every other key is a section of label: value pairs, named after the section heading (`sample_print_conditions`, `recommended_printing_conditions`, ...). Every block names the page it was read from.

issued.description: Date as printed, or the words saying it is not printed.

normalised.description: Typed values. Every key other than the fixed four ends in its unit (`_c`, `_mpa`, `_pct`, `_g_cm3`, `_g_10min`, `_mm_s`, `_mm`, `_kj_m2`) and holds a field object that names where the number was read. Print-direction keys carry `_xy` or `_z` before the unit. Sample print settings are flat keys (`sample_print_nozzle_c`, `sample_print_bed_c`, `sample_print_speed_mm_s`, `sample_print_infill_pct`), one field per number, so every number has its own page and row.

note.description: How these values relate to `tds` or `spool_rfid` (transcription only, no conversion).

shrinkage_pct.description: null until a calibration measurement exists; a vendor TDS that says 'low shrinkage' gives no number.

marketing_claims.description: Store-page text, not test data. Kept only so a claim can be traced; nothing here is a property.

flags.description: Everything a reviewer must read before accepting: mislabelled rows, re-keyed values, values the extractor dropped, where a fact came from when the TDS lacks it. Empty is allowed and means the pipeline and the hand-check found nothing to say.

reviewed.description: ISO date of the review that set `status`.

citation.description: A citation string in one of the forms scripts/validate.py accepts under --strict.

tds_rows.description: One object per table row, cells verbatim, in document order.

row.description: Row number in the extracted document, counted across all tables; what `normalised.*.row` points at.

tds_section.description: A label: value table or block, values as printed.

field.description: One transcribed number (or range) and where it was read. At least one of value, min, max; and either a page in the cited document or a stated basis.

at_c.description: Temperature the value was measured at, when the document prints one.

as_printed.description: The original cell text when a bound was taken from a word (e.g. 'Normal-60℃').

basis.description: Where the number comes from when it is not a page of the cited document (e.g. an RFID tag field).

label_in_document.description: The row label when the key name differs from it.
